# Adjudication Task — Chapter 454

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃454화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|눈을 부릅뜬 채 굳어 있던 청년, 아니 주원공이 떨리는 목소리로 물었다.
  6|
  7|“뭐, 뭐라?”
  8|
  9|이놈은 아까부터 귓구멍이 막혔나. 자꾸 했던 말을 반복하게 만드네.
 10|
 11|입을 딱 벌린 채 나와 주원공을 번갈아 바라보는 사람들의 시선을 무시하며 재차 입을 열었다.
 12|
 13|“내리라고.”
 14|
 15|“나, 난 주원공이다!”
 16|
 17|“주인공이든 주원공이든. 내려.”
 18|
 19|“네놈도 결국 대국의 백성일진대, 황상 폐하의 혈족인 내게 어찌 이리도 무례를 범할 수 있단 말이냐!”
 20|
 21|“내 친구 중에 존슨이라고 있거든? 그 사람 있었으면 다른 걸 범했을 거야.”
 22|
 23|“……!”
 24|
 25|“마지막으로 말한다. 내려.”
 26|
 27|무슨 소리인지는 몰라도 사람이라면 누구나 위험을 감지하는 법.
 28|
 29|본능적으로 엉덩이를 움찔거리던 주원공이 슬그머니 몸을 일으켰다.
 30|
 31|하지만 생전 경험해 본 적 없는 상황에 불안한 듯 눈동자를 굴리면서도, 황족이라는 배경을 믿는지 마지막까지 엄포를 놓는 걸 잊지 않았다.
 32|
 33|“이, 이러고도 무사할 것 같으냐!”
 34|
 35|“어, 무사할 것 같은데.”
 36|
 37|“황족을 능멸하다니, 이건 역모다!”
 38|
 39|“탈모만 아니면 돼.”
 40|
 41|“뭐 이런 놈이……!”
 42|
 43|아무렇지 않게 대꾸했지만, 크게 틀린 말은 아니다.
 44|
 45|천자(天子)와 같은 주씨 성에 용의 핏줄을 타고난 자. 그 자체로 존귀한 것이 황족이니까.
 46|
 47|비록 무림과 관부가 상호불가침의 관계라는 해도 황족에 대한 무례와 위협은 중죄로 취급받는다.
 48|
 49|괜히 아까부터 제갈세가 가솔이 똥 마려운 강아지처럼 끙끙거리는 것이 아니다.
 50|
 51|“그, 이제 그만하시는 편이 좋을 듯합니다.”
 52|
 53|나는 가솔의 속삭임에 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
 54|
 55|“왜요?”
 56|
 57|“예, 예?”
 58|
 59|“제가 뭐 했어요? 욕을 한 것도 아니고, 그렇다고 죽인다고 협박한 것도 아닌데. 심지어 공격도 저쪽에서 먼저 했어요. 전 사인교에서만 내리라고 한 거고.”
 60|
 61|“……아니, 뭐. 따지고 보면 그건 맞는데. 그래도 황족 아닙니까.”
 62|
 63|“황족도 황족 나름이지, 팔촌이면 같은 핏줄이 아니라 그냥 피 몇 방울 떨어트린 수준 아닙니까? 당장 제가 장강에 침 좀 뱉으면 저랑 장강이랑 팔촌 정도는 될 것 같은데.”
 64|
 65|“헉. 진 대협, 제발.”
 66|
 67|“괜찮아요. 어차피 작게 말해서 아무도 못 들었을 테니까.”
 68|
 69|그때, 나와 가솔이 속닥거리는 모습을 착각한 주원공이 기세등등한 목소리로 외쳤다.
 70|
 71|“이제야 사태를 파악한 모양이군. 하지만 이미 늦었다. 곧 황실의 십만 대군이 출동하여 네놈을 포함한 역도들의 구족(九族)을 멸할 것이니!”
 72|
 73|“오, 버스터 콜.”
 74|
 75|“아까부터 뭐라는 것이냐, 이 역적놈아!”
 76|
 77|“헉!”
 78|
 79|“히이익!”
 80|
 81|주원공의 눈에 숨길 수 없는 분노가 깃들자, 양민들이 헛숨을 삼키며 바닥에 넙죽 엎드렸다. 이미 곳곳에서는 도망치는 이들까지 속출했다.
 82|
 83|괜한 일에 연루되는 것을 피하려는 모양인데, 보는 눈이 적어지는 셈이니 내 입장에서도 나쁠 건 없었다.
 84|
 85|‘그나저나 이것들은 심심하면 구족을 들이미네.’
 86|
 87|구족 이하로는 취급을 안 해 주나?
 88|
 89|한숨을 푹 내쉬는 내게 제갈세가의 가솔이 속삭였다.
 90|
 91|“너무 겁먹지는 마십시오. 십만 대군 운운한 것은 허세니까요.”
 92|
 93|“……제가 바봅니까? 그걸 믿게.”
 94|
 95|“애초에 주 공자는 황족의 권위를 내세워 재산을 착복하다가 귀양 온 상태라, 일을 키울 생각은 없을 겁니다. 그러니 적당한 선에서 사과하고 물러나시지요.”
 96|
 97|“잠깐만. 귀양?”
 98|
 99|“예.”
100|
101|“저게?”
102|
103|“황족이잖습니까. 아무리 먼 방계라고는 해도 핏줄은 무시 못 합니다. 게다가 황위 계승 서열과는 거리가 먼 방계라, 죄를 지어도 적당한 향응을 누릴 수 있게 해 주는 것이지요.”
104|
105|“요컨대, 하도 좆밥이라 주위에서 신경도 안 쓴다?”
106|
107|“……진 대협, 제발 말씀을 좀 가려서 하십시오.”
108|
109|나는 가솔의 푸념을 한 귀로 흘려들으며 피식 웃었다.
110|
111|황족씩이나 되는 놈이 왜 황궁이 아니라 호북성 대로변에서 망나니들과 친목질을 하고 있나 했더니, 생각했던 것 이상으로 별 볼 일 없는 놈이었다.
112|
113|뭐, 팔촌 운운했을 때부터 짐작했던 거긴 하지만.
114|
115|“우선 존귀한 이 몸을 알아보지 못한 네 놈의 그 오만한 눈깔을 파 버리고, 오체분시를 한 다음……!”
116|
117|“그래. 알겠으니까 그다음은 이거나 보고 다시 이야기하자고.”
118|
119|나는 일장 연설을 쏟아내는 주원공을 향해, 품에서 꺼낸 물건을 던졌다.
120|
121|동시에 가슴을 한껏 펴고 있던 놈이 양팔을 허우적거리며 주저앉았다.
122|
123|“암기다! 암기! 이놈이 황족을 시해하려 한다!”
124|
125|“……수준 상당하네, 진짜.”
126|
127|그리고 다음 순간.
128|
129|주원공의 발 앞에 툭, 하고 떨어진 ‘암기’가 모두의 시선 속에서 찬란한 빛을 흩뿌렸다.
130|
131|“어?”
132|
133|의문 어린 눈빛으로 자신의 발 앞에 놓인 물건을 바라보던 주원공이 멍하니 입을 벌렸다.
134|
135|“어? 어어, 어어어어!”
136|
137|물음표가 느낌표로, 분노가 경악으로 바뀌기까지는 그리 오랜 시간이 걸리지 않았다.
138|
139|구름과 용이 음각된 상산왕 주표의 증표와 나를 번갈아 바라보던 주원공이 무겁게 입을 뗐다.
140|
141|“내 자비를 베풀어, 그대를 용서하겠노라.”
142|
143|“…….”
144|
145|지랄한다.
146|
147|
148|
149|* * *
150|
151|
152|
153|“그래서, 동정호 가는 길이셨다고?”
154|
155|“그렇다! 아니, 그렇소!”
156|
157|내 부드러운 음성에 주원공이 힘차게 고개를 끄덕였다.
158|
159|그가 고용한 청협방의 꽃 병풍들은 뒤늦게 도착한 관군들과 함께 사람들을 입단속 시키고 있었고, 기어코 만두 대량 구매에 성공한 청풍은 동정호라는 말에 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
160|
161|“와아, 동정호!”
162|
163|비로소 이 만두 귀신의 신분을 알게 된 주원공이 불안한 눈빛으로 청풍의 허리춤에 찬 검을 힐끗거렸다.
164|
165|“그, 그대가 원한다면 초대해 줄 수도 있소만…….”
166|
167|내가 중얼거렸다.
168|
169|“마음에도 없는 소릴 하시네.”
170|
171|“착각이다! 아니, 착각이오.”
172|
173|“그럼 평소에도 착각을 자주 하는 성격이신가? 조용히 지나가려는 사람도 공격하는 걸 보면 그런 것 같기도 하고.”
174|
175|“그건…… 내 다시 한번 사과드리리다. 상산왕 전하의 증표를 갖고 계신 줄은 꿈에도 몰랐소.”
176|
177|“아, 증표가 없었으면 십만 대군을 끌고 와서 구족을 멸하고, 눈깔 뽑은 다음 오체분시를 했을 것이다?”
178|
179|“무, 무슨 그런 말씀을. 허, 허허허.”
180|
181|억지로 웃는 모습이 안쓰러울 지경이다.
182|
183|‘나도 증표의 효과가 이 정도일 줄은 몰랐는데.’
184|
185|주원공이 이토록 저자세로 나오는 데에는 다 이유가 있었다.
186|
187|동물도 순종, 잡종을 따지는데 천하에서 가장 고귀한 핏줄이라는 황족은 오죽하겠나.
188|
189|같은 황실의 피가 흐른다고 해도 상산왕 주표는 천자의 하나뿐인 동복동생이자, 그가 직접 임명한 유일한 번왕(藩王)이기도 하다.
190|
191|선황 사후, 제위를 둘러싼 다툼에서 수많은 핏줄을 제거한 냉혹한 황제의 아픈 손가락이 바로 상산왕 주표다.
192|
193|반면 주원공은 팔촌이나 떨어진 방계 황족.
194|
195|직계 황족이 가진 정통성과 권위. 촌수로 따져도 주원공에게 있어 상산왕 주표는 까마득하게 높은 집안 어르신인 것이다.
196|
197|‘이런 걸 이이제이(以夷制夷)라고 하는 거지.’
198|
199|오랑캐는 오랑캐로 무찌르고, 약한 천룡인은 강한 천룡인으로 무찌르는 법.
200|
201|내 열렬한 팬클럽 회장이 이 정도라니, 정말이지 생각할수록 가슴이 웅장해진다.
202|
203|“뭐, 아무튼 그건 그렇다 치고. 동정호에는 가서 뭐 하시려고?”
204|
205|“그, 그게. 날씨가 좋아서 뱃놀이를 좀…….”
206|
207|어이없어하는 내 표정에 주원공이 황급히 말을 고쳤다.
208|
209|“뱃놀이 겸, 요새 호북성의 분위기가 영 좋지 않다고 하니 민생을 살피려고 했소.”
210|
211|“……그전에 본인 인생부터 살펴야 하지 않을까. 뒷구멍으로 한 재산 빼돌리다가 귀양 오신 거라며?”
212|
213|“큼, 크흠!”
214|
215|“그런데 사람들을 이렇게 잔뜩 끌어모아서 뱃놀이를 가? 그것도 이 시국에?”
216|
217|호북성에 눈 있고 귀 달린 이들은 최근 끊이지 않는 흉흉한 소문에 불안에 떠는데, 귀양 온 황족이란 놈은 동정호에서 초호화 뱃놀이라니.
218|
219|이시국 씨가 들었으면 오함마로 골통을 깨부숴도 할 말이 없다.
220|
221|‘하여간에 있는 것들이란.’
222|
223|고개를 절레절레 저은 나는 자리에서 일어났다.
224|
225|적당히 잡음 없이 마무리되었으니 더는 신경 쓰지 않고 떠날 생각이었는데, 주원공의 눈에는 다르게 비친 모양이었다.
226|
227|“자, 잠깐만. 어딜 가시는 거요?”
228|
229|“동정호에 뱃놀이하러 가는 것보다는 바쁜 몸이라. 왜 그러시는데?”
230|
231|“마음 상했다면 내 다시 한번 사과드리겠소. 그런 의미에서…….”
232|
233|말꼬리를 흐린 주원공이 눈짓하자, 미리 준비하고 있던 청협방의 무인들이 행렬 사이사이 위치한 화려한 가마를 메고 왔다.
234|
235|천을 걷지도 않았는데, 은은한 향기가 코끝을 파고든다.
236|
237|‘이거 설마.’
238|
239|옛말에 그런 속담이 있다. 설마가 사람 잡는다. 이번에도 마찬가지였다.
240|
241|“모습을 보이거라.”
242|
243|주원공의 말이 떨어지기가 무섭게 가마의 문이 스르륵 열렸다.
244|
245|그리고 다음 순간, 조심스럽게 가마에서 내리는 한 여인의 모습에 나도 모르게 한 줄기 탄성이 입술을 비집고 흘러나왔다.
246|
247|“……허.”
248|
249|흔히들 연예인을 두고 예쁘다, 잘생겼다고들 말한다.
250|
251|하지만 눈앞의 이 여인은, 그런 세간의 기준을 뛰어넘는 무엇인가가 있었다.
252|
253|‘아름답다.’
254|
255|그래, 아마도 이 표현이 가장 적당할 것이다.
256|
257|여인은 그 정도로 아름다웠다. 이미 주원공의 속셈을 짐작했던 나조차도 감탄할 만큼.
258|
259|궁기방이 황급히 침으로 세수를 하고, 혁무진이 넋을 놓을 만큼. 고기만두와 야채만두를 양손에 올려두고 고민하던 청풍이 만두를 모조리 떨어트릴 만큼 대단한 미모였다.
260|
261|잔잔하게 흐르는 충격 속에서 주원공의 목소리가 들려왔다.
262|
263|“본인이 곁에 두고 있는 가기(歌妓)요. 보시다시피 그 용모는 가히 천하절색이라 부를 만하고, 음율을 다루는 솜씨가 뛰어나 이 아이의 연주를 들으면 모두가 넋을 놓지.”
264|
265|글쎄, 굳이 연주가 없어도 사람의 혼을 쏙 빼놓을 것 같은데.
266|
267|숨길 수 없는 감탄이 드러난 내 표정에 피식 웃은 주원공이 여인에게 말했다.
268|
269|“무엇 하느냐? 어서 인사 올리지 않고.”
270|
271|붉은 입술이 천천히 열렸다.
272|
273|“소녀, 홍란(紅蘭)이라 합니다. 귀인을 뵙게 되어 기쁘기 한량없습니다.”
274|
275|“……오.”
276|
277|“……와.”
278|

[P76]
Ju Wongong nodded vigorously at my gentle tone.

[P77]
The decorative showpieces from Qingxia Hall whom he had hired were warning people to keep their mouths shut alongside the government troops, who had arrived late. Meanwhile, Cheongpung, who had somehow succeeded in buying dumplings in bulk, opened his eyes wide at the mention of Dongting Lake.

[P78]
“Wow! Dongting Lake!”

[P79]
Now that Ju Wongong knew the identity of this dumpling ghost, he glanced uneasily at the sword hanging from Cheongpung’s waist.

[P80]
“W-well, I could invite you along if you wished…”

[P81]
I muttered,

[P82]
“You don’t mean that at all.”

[P83]
“That is a misunderstanding! No, I mean, you misunderstand.”

[P84]
“Do you misunderstand things this often? Considering you attacked people who were trying to pass by peacefully, it certainly seems that way.”

[P85]
“That was… I shall apologize once again. I never dreamed that you possessed His Highness Prince Shangshan’s token.”

[P86]
“Oh, I see. So if I hadn’t had the token, you would’ve brought a hundred thousand troops to exterminate nine branches of my family, gouged out my eyes, and torn me limb from limb?”

[P87]
“W-why would you say such a thing? Ha, ha-ha-ha.”

[P88]
His forced laughter was almost pitiful.

[P89]
*I didn’t know the token would have this much power either.*

[P90]
There was a reason Ju Wongong had become so submissive.

[P91]
Even animals were judged as purebred or mixed-breed. How much more would the imperial family—the noblest bloodline in the world—care about such distinctions?

[P92]
Though the same imperial blood ran through their veins, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was the Son of Heaven’s one and only full brother and the only vassal prince the Emperor had personally appointed.

[P93]
After the late Emperor’s death, the ruthless man who now sat upon the throne had eliminated countless blood relatives in the struggle for succession. Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was that ruthless Emperor’s one soft spot.

[P94]
Ju Wongong, on the other hand, came from a collateral branch eight degrees removed.

[P95]
The direct imperial line possessed legitimacy and authority. Even by degrees of kinship, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was an exalted elder of the family, far beyond Ju Wongong’s reach.

[P96]
*This is what they call using barbarians to defeat barbarians.*

[P97]
Defeat barbarians with barbarians, and a weak Celestial Dragon with a strong Celestial Dragon.

[P98]
The chairman of my fan club was this formidable. Just thinking about it made my heart swell.

[P99]
“Well, putting that aside, what are you planning to do at Dongting Lake?”

[P100]
“W-well, the weather is pleasant, so I thought I might go boating…”

[P101]
At my incredulous expression, Ju Wongong hurriedly corrected himself.

[P102]
“I intended to go boating while also inspecting the people’s welfare, since I heard the mood in Hubei Province has been rather grim lately.”

[P103]
“……Shouldn’t you inspect your own life first? I heard you were exiled for siphoning off a fortune through back channels.”

[P104]
“Ahem! Ahem!”

[P105]
“And you brought all these people along for a boat ride? At a time like this?”

[P106]
Everyone in Hubei Province with eyes and ears was trembling with anxiety over the grim rumors that refused to die down, yet this exiled imperial relative was planning a lavish boating excursion on Dongting Lake.

[P107]
If Mr. Current Situation heard about this and smashed Ju Wongong’s skull with a sledgehammer, Ju Wongong would have no right to complain.

[P108]
*That’s rich people for you.*

[P109]
I shook my head and rose from my seat.

[P110]
The matter had been settled without too much fuss, so I intended to leave and forget about it. Ju Wongong seemed to take it differently.

[P111]
“W-wait a moment. Where are you going?”

[P112]
“I’m a busy man. I have more important things to do than go boating on Dongting Lake. Why?”

[P113]
“If I have offended you, I shall apologize once again. And in that spirit…”

[P114]
Ju Wongong trailed off and gave a meaningful glance.

[P115]
The Qingxia Hall martial artists who had been waiting for his signal carried over one of the ornate sedan chairs positioned throughout the procession.

[P116]
They hadn’t even drawn back its curtains, yet a faint fragrance drifted into my nose.

[P117]
*Don’t tell me…*

[P118]
There was an old saying that the thing you dismissed with “surely not” was the thing most likely to get you. This time was no different.

[P119]
“Show yourself.”

[P120]
The moment Ju Wongong spoke, the sedan chair’s door slid open.

[P121]
A woman carefully stepped down, and an exclamation escaped my lips before I could stop it.

[P122]
“……Whoa.”

[P123]
People often described celebrities as pretty or handsome.

[P124]
But the woman before me possessed something beyond those ordinary standards.

[P125]
*Beautiful.*

[P126]
Yes. That was probably the right word.

[P127]
She was beautiful enough to draw admiration even from me, despite the fact that I had already guessed Ju Wongong’s intentions.

[P128]
Beautiful enough to make Gung Gibang hurriedly wash his face with spit and Hyuk Mujin stare in a daze. Beautiful enough to make Cheongpung—who had been holding a meat dumpling in one hand and a vegetable dumpling in the other, trying to choose between them—drop them both.

[P129]
As the quiet shock rippled through the crowd, Ju Wongong’s voice reached me.

[P130]
“She is the singing courtesan I keep at my side. As you can see, her beauty deserves to be called unrivaled beneath the heavens. She is also extraordinarily skilled in music. Anyone who hears her play loses himself completely.”

[P131]
I wasn’t so sure she needed the music. She looked capable of stealing a person’s soul without playing a single note.

[P132]
Ju Wongong laughed quietly at the admiration plain on my face, then turned to the woman.

[P133]
“What are you waiting for? Hurry and greet him.”

[P134]
Her red lips slowly parted.

[P135]
“This humble girl is called Honglan. It is my greatest pleasure to meet such an honored guest.”

[P136]
“……Oh.”

[P137]
“……Wow.”

[P138]
“……Amazing.”

[P139]
Before the shock of her appearance had even faded, exclamations burst out from every direction.

[P140]
Her voice was clear and pure, yet alluring.

[P141]
Honglan. Red Orchid. The name suited her better than anyone.

[P142]
*Of course, it wasn’t her real name, and she wasn’t an ordinary singing courtesan either.*

[P143]
Like most courtesans, including Wolhwa, Honglan concealed her true name.

[P144]
And unlike Ju Wongong, who knew absolutely nothing about martial arts, she had received at least some training.

[P145]
—Lower District Sect?

[P146]
Her slender shoulders twitched at my Sound Transmission. Then Honglan gave the slightest nod.

[P147]
*The Lower District Sect. I had a feeling that was it.*

[P148]
The Lower District Sect had more disciples than any organization apart from the Beggars’ Sect.

[P149]
Ju Wongong didn’t seem aware of it, but like the Lower District Sect’s other courtesans, Honglan had learned enough martial arts to protect herself.

[P150]
“So? What do you think, Great Hero Jin? Give me the opportunity, and this Young Master will treat you properly. Of course, Honglan will sit beside you…”

[P151]
*Let’s see you refuse to come along after this.*

[P152]
The words were written plainly across Ju Wongong’s smug face.

[P153]
I gazed at Honglan for a moment, then smiled.

[P154]
“Forget it. Let’s each continue on our way.”

[P155]
“Then we can all go somewhere else together—hm? W-wait. What did you just say?”

[P156]
“Why are you so surprised? I’m pretty sure I already said I had something urgent to do. Is my memory failing me?”

[P157]
“N-no. But Honglan is here…”

[P158]
I raised a hand and cut Ju Wongong off.

[P159]
I had already wasted enough time getting dragged into this nonsense. If I were the kind of man who lost his head over a beautiful woman and followed her wherever she went, I wouldn’t have survived this long.

[P160]
“Don’t overdo the partying. You’d be better off going home and keeping your head down. See you.”

[P161]
I was about to turn away when Ju Wongong held something out to me.

[P162]
“Wait! Then at least this.”

[P163]
“……?”

[P164]
“I heard that His Highness Prince Shangshan received your autograph, Great Hero Jin. Please give me one as well…”

[P165]
“……!”

[P166]
At this rate, my fan café would be reaching Leaf Level 2 soon.[^1]

[P167]
[^1]: Korean online fan communities often use graded membership tiers named after stages of a leaf’s growth.
```

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Though the same imperial blood ran through their veins, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was the Son of Heaven’s one and only full brother and the only vassal prince the Emperor had personally appointed.

[P93]
After the late Emperor’s death, the ruthless man who now sat upon the throne had eliminated countless blood relatives in the struggle for succession. Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was that ruthless Emperor’s one soft spot.

[P94]
Ju Wongong, on the other hand, came from a collateral branch eight degrees removed.

[P95]
The direct imperial line possessed legitimacy and authority. Even by degrees of kinship, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was an exalted elder of the family, far beyond Ju Wongong’s reach.

[P96]
*This is what they call using barbarians to defeat barbarians.*

[P97]
Defeat barbarians with barbarians, and a weak Celestial Dragon with a strong Celestial Dragon.

[P98]
The chairman of my fan club was this formidable. Just thinking about it made my heart swell.

[P99]
“Well, putting that aside, what are you planning to do at Dongting Lake?”

[P100]
“W-well, the weather is pleasant, so I thought I might go boating…”

[P101]
At my incredulous expression, Ju Wongong hurriedly corrected himself.

[P102]
“I intended to go boating while also inspecting the people’s welfare, since I heard the mood in Hubei Province has been rather grim lately.”

[P103]
“……Shouldn’t you inspect your own life first? I heard you were exiled for siphoning off a fortune through back channels.”

[P104]
“Ahem! Ahem!”

[P105]
“And you brought all these people along for a boat ride? At a time like this?”

[P106]
Everyone in Hubei Province with eyes and ears was trembling with anxiety over the grim rumors that refused to die down, yet this exiled imperial relative was planning a lavish boating excursion on Dongting Lake.

[P107]
If Mr. Current Situation heard about this and smashed Ju Wongong’s skull with a sledgehammer, Ju Wongong would have no right to complain.

[P108]
*That’s rich people for you.*

[P109]
I shook my head and rose from my seat.

[P110]
The matter had been settled without too much fuss, so I intended to leave and forget about it. Ju Wongong seemed to take it differently.

[P111]
“W-wait a moment. Where are you going?”

[P112]
“I’m a busy man. I have more important things to do than go boating on Dongting Lake. Why?”

[P113]
“If I have offended you, I shall apologize once again. And in that spirit…”

[P114]
Ju Wongong trailed off and gave a meaningful glance.

[P115]
The Qingxia Hall martial artists who had been waiting for his signal carried over one of the ornate sedan chairs positioned throughout the procession.

[P116]
They hadn’t even drawn back its curtains, yet a faint fragrance drifted into my nose.

[P117]
*Don’t tell me…*

[P118]
There was an old saying that the thing you dismissed with “surely not” was the thing most likely to get you. This time was no different.

[P119]
“Show yourself.”

[P120]
The moment Ju Wongong spoke, the sedan chair’s door slid open.

[P121]
A woman carefully stepped down, and an exclamation escaped my lips before I could stop it.

[P122]
“……Whoa.”

[P123]
People often described celebrities as pretty or handsome.

[P124]
But the woman before me possessed something beyond those ordinary standards.

[P125]
*Beautiful.*

[P126]
Yes. That was probably the right word.

[P127]
She was beautiful enough to draw admiration even from me, despite the fact that I had already guessed Ju Wongong’s intentions.

[P128]
Beautiful enough to make Gung Gibang hurriedly wash his face with spit and Hyuk Mujin stare in a daze. Beautiful enough to make Cheongpung—who had been holding a meat dumpling in one hand and a vegetable dumpling in the other, trying to choose between them—drop them both.

[P129]
As the quiet shock rippled through the crowd, Ju Wongong’s voice reached me.

[P130]
“She is the singing courtesan I keep at my side. As you can see, her beauty deserves to be called unrivaled beneath the heavens. She is also extraordinarily skilled in music. Anyone who hears her play loses himself completely.”

[P131]
I wasn’t so sure she needed the music. She looked capable of stealing a person’s soul without playing a single note.

[P132]
Ju Wongong laughed quietly at the admiration plain on my face, then turned to the woman.

[P133]
“What are you waiting for? Hurry and greet him.”

[P134]
Her red lips slowly parted.

[P135]
“This humble girl is called Honglan. It is my greatest pleasure to meet such an honored guest.”

[P136]
“……Oh.”

[P137]
“……Wow.”

[P138]
“……Amazing.”

[P139]
Before the shock of her appearance had even faded, exclamations burst out from every direction.

[P140]
Her voice was clear and pure, yet alluring.

[P141]
Honglan. Red Orchid. The name suited her better than anyone.

[P142]
*Of course, it wasn’t her real name, and she wasn’t an ordinary singing courtesan either.*

[P143]
Like most courtesans, including Wolhwa, Honglan concealed her true name.

[P144]
And unlike Ju Wongong, who knew absolutely nothing about martial arts, she had received at least some training.

[P145]
—Lower District Sect?

[P146]
Her slender shoulders twitched at my Sound Transmission. Then Honglan gave the slightest nod.

[P147]
*The Lower District Sect. I had a feeling that was it.*

[P148]
The Lower District Sect had more disciples than any organization apart from the Beggars’ Sect.

[P149]
Ju Wongong didn’t seem aware of it, but like the Lower District Sect’s other courtesans, Honglan had learned enough martial arts to protect herself.

[P150]
“So? What do you think, Great Hero Jin? Give me the opportunity, and this Young Master will treat you properly. Of course, Honglan will sit beside you…”

[P151]
*Let’s see you refuse to come along after this.*

[P152]
The words were written plainly across Ju Wongong’s smug face.

[P153]
I gazed at Honglan for a moment, then smiled.

[P154]
“Forget it. Let’s each continue on our way.”

[P155]
“Then we can all go somewhere else together—hm? W-wait. What did you just say?”

[P156]
“Why are you so surprised? I’m pretty sure I already said I had something urgent to do. Is my memory failing me?”

[P157]
“N-no. But Honglan is here…”

[P158]
I raised a hand and cut Ju Wongong off.

[P159]
I had already wasted enough time getting dragged into this nonsense. If I were the kind of man who lost his head over a beautiful woman and followed her wherever she went, I wouldn’t have survived this long.

[P160]
“Don’t overdo the partying. You’d be better off going home and keeping your head down. See you.”

[P161]
I was about to turn away when Ju Wongong held something out to me.

[P162]
“Wait! Then at least this.”

[P163]
“……?”

[P164]
“I heard that His Highness Prince Shangshan received your autograph, Great Hero Jin. Please give me one as well…”

[P165]
“……!”

[P166]
At this rate, my fan café would be reaching Leaf Level 2 soon.[^1]

[P167]
[^1]: Korean online fan communities often use graded membership tiers named after stages of a leaf’s growth.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 454

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃454화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|눈을 부릅뜬 채 굳어 있던 청년, 아니 주원공이 떨리는 목소리로 물었다.
  6|
  7|“뭐, 뭐라?”
  8|
  9|이놈은 아까부터 귓구멍이 막혔나. 자꾸 했던 말을 반복하게 만드네.
 10|
 11|입을 딱 벌린 채 나와 주원공을 번갈아 바라보는 사람들의 시선을 무시하며 재차 입을 열었다.
 12|
 13|“내리라고.”
 14|
 15|“나, 난 주원공이다!”
 16|
 17|“주인공이든 주원공이든. 내려.”
 18|
 19|“네놈도 결국 대국의 백성일진대, 황상 폐하의 혈족인 내게 어찌 이리도 무례를 범할 수 있단 말이냐!”
 20|
 21|“내 친구 중에 존슨이라고 있거든? 그 사람 있었으면 다른 걸 범했을 거야.”
 22|
 23|“……!”
 24|
 25|“마지막으로 말한다. 내려.”
 26|
 27|무슨 소리인지는 몰라도 사람이라면 누구나 위험을 감지하는 법.
 28|
 29|본능적으로 엉덩이를 움찔거리던 주원공이 슬그머니 몸을 일으켰다.
 30|
 31|하지만 생전 경험해 본 적 없는 상황에 불안한 듯 눈동자를 굴리면서도, 황족이라는 배경을 믿는지 마지막까지 엄포를 놓는 걸 잊지 않았다.
 32|
 33|“이, 이러고도 무사할 것 같으냐!”
 34|
 35|“어, 무사할 것 같은데.”
 36|
 37|“황족을 능멸하다니, 이건 역모다!”
 38|
 39|“탈모만 아니면 돼.”
 40|
 41|“뭐 이런 놈이……!”
 42|
 43|아무렇지 않게 대꾸했지만, 크게 틀린 말은 아니다.
 44|
 45|천자(天子)와 같은 주씨 성에 용의 핏줄을 타고난 자. 그 자체로 존귀한 것이 황족이니까.
 46|
 47|비록 무림과 관부가 상호불가침의 관계라는 해도 황족에 대한 무례와 위협은 중죄로 취급받는다.
 48|
 49|괜히 아까부터 제갈세가 가솔이 똥 마려운 강아지처럼 끙끙거리는 것이 아니다.
 50|
 51|“그, 이제 그만하시는 편이 좋을 듯합니다.”
 52|
 53|나는 가솔의 속삭임에 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
 54|
 55|“왜요?”
 56|
 57|“예, 예?”
 58|
 59|“제가 뭐 했어요? 욕을 한 것도 아니고, 그렇다고 죽인다고 협박한 것도 아닌데. 심지어 공격도 저쪽에서 먼저 했어요. 전 사인교에서만 내리라고 한 거고.”
 60|
 61|“……아니, 뭐. 따지고 보면 그건 맞는데. 그래도 황족 아닙니까.”
 62|
 63|“황족도 황족 나름이지, 팔촌이면 같은 핏줄이 아니라 그냥 피 몇 방울 떨어트린 수준 아닙니까? 당장 제가 장강에 침 좀 뱉으면 저랑 장강이랑 팔촌 정도는 될 것 같은데.”
 64|
 65|“헉. 진 대협, 제발.”
 66|
 67|“괜찮아요. 어차피 작게 말해서 아무도 못 들었을 테니까.”
 68|
 69|그때, 나와 가솔이 속닥거리는 모습을 착각한 주원공이 기세등등한 목소리로 외쳤다.
 70|
 71|“이제야 사태를 파악한 모양이군. 하지만 이미 늦었다. 곧 황실의 십만 대군이 출동하여 네놈을 포함한 역도들의 구족(九族)을 멸할 것이니!”
 72|
 73|“오, 버스터 콜.”
 74|
 75|“아까부터 뭐라는 것이냐, 이 역적놈아!”
 76|
 77|“헉!”
 78|
 79|“히이익!”
 80|
 81|주원공의 눈에 숨길 수 없는 분노가 깃들자, 양민들이 헛숨을 삼키며 바닥에 넙죽 엎드렸다. 이미 곳곳에서는 도망치는 이들까지 속출했다.
 82|
 83|괜한 일에 연루되는 것을 피하려는 모양인데, 보는 눈이 적어지는 셈이니 내 입장에서도 나쁠 건 없었다.
 84|
 85|‘그나저나 이것들은 심심하면 구족을 들이미네.’
 86|
 87|구족 이하로는 취급을 안 해 주나?
 88|
 89|한숨을 푹 내쉬는 내게 제갈세가의 가솔이 속삭였다.
 90|
 91|“너무 겁먹지는 마십시오. 십만 대군 운운한 것은 허세니까요.”
 92|
 93|“……제가 바봅니까? 그걸 믿게.”
 94|
 95|“애초에 주 공자는 황족의 권위를 내세워 재산을 착복하다가 귀양 온 상태라, 일을 키울 생각은 없을 겁니다. 그러니 적당한 선에서 사과하고 물러나시지요.”
 96|
 97|“잠깐만. 귀양?”
 98|
 99|“예.”
100|
101|“저게?”
102|
103|“황족이잖습니까. 아무리 먼 방계라고는 해도 핏줄은 무시 못 합니다. 게다가 황위 계승 서열과는 거리가 먼 방계라, 죄를 지어도 적당한 향응을 누릴 수 있게 해 주는 것이지요.”
104|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
